chunks.arabic_text: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ، أَبُو الْعَبَّاسِ، الرَّازِيُّ، صَاحِبُ كِتَابِ "الشِّفَاءِ وَالْجَلَاءِ". كَانَ ضَعِيفًا. وَحَدَّثَنِي أَبِي (رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ) أَنَّهُ كَانَ فِي مَذْهَبِهِ ارْتِفَاعٌ. وَحَدِيثُهُ يُعْرَفُ تُرًا، وَيُنْكَرُ أُخْرَى.

translations.en: Ahmad ibn Ali, Abu al-Abbas, al-Razi, the author of the book "Al-Shifa wa al-Jala". He was weak. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) informed me that in his madhhab there was elevation (height/standing). His hadith is recognized sometimes, and rejected other times.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Duafa* characterizes Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi as a weak narrator whose hadiths are subject to fluctuating acceptance, a status often linked to theological deviations. The specific mention of 'elevation' (irtifa') in his madhhab likely alludes to the Shia concept of *ta'li* (exaltation of the Imams), suggesting his weakness may stem from specific doctrinal nuances rather than mere memory loss. This highlights the critical Shia methodology of distinguishing between minor narrational defects and significant theological errors when evaluating a scholar's reliability.
en.seo_question: Who is Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi and what is his status in his hadith?

key_terms.ارْتِفَاعٌ: elevation or height (often referring to standing or status)
